title: The café with no queue
setting: A Saturday afternoon on a busy shopping street. Yuki and her coworker and friend Mai have been out shopping, and Mai has stocked up on cat food. They'd planned to finish the day at a pancake place they'd been talking about.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mai, daijoubu? nimotsu, hitotsu motou ka?
lines.ja: マイ、大丈夫？荷物、一つ持とうか？
lines.kana: まい、だいじょうぶ？にもつ、ひとつもとうか？
lines.english: Mai, you okay? Want me to carry one of your bags?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: ii no? arigatou. neko no gohan takusan katchatte, nimotsu sugoku omoi n da.
lines.ja: いいの？ありがとう。猫のごはんたくさん買っちゃって、荷物すごく重いんだ。
lines.kana: いいの？ありがとう。ねこのごはんたくさんかっちゃって、にもつすごくおもいんだ。
lines.english: Are you sure? Thanks. I went and bought loads of cat food, so my bags are really heavy.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: uwa, honto da. nanka kyou, hito ooi ne.
lines.ja: うわ、ほんとだ。なんか今日、人多いね。
lines.kana: うわ、ほんとだ。なんかきょう、ひとおおいね。
lines.english: Whoa, they really are. It's kind of crowded today, isn't it?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: doyoubi da kara ne. a, hora, ano pankeeki no omise, metcha naranderu.
lines.ja: 土曜日だからね。あ、ほら、あのパンケーキのお店、めっちゃ並んでる。
lines.kana: どようびだからね。あ、ほら、あのぱんけーきのおみせ、めっちゃならんでる。
lines.english: Well, it is Saturday. Oh, look, there's a huge line at that pancake place.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, are, ikou tte itteta omise ja nai?
lines.ja: え、あれ、行こうって言ってたお店じゃない？
lines.kana: え、あれ、いこうっていってたおみせじゃない？
lines.english: Wait, isn't that the place we said we'd go to?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sou. saikin, sugoku ninki aru n da tte.
lines.ja: そう。最近、すごく人気あるんだって。
lines.kana: そう。さいきん、すごくにんきあるんだって。
lines.english: Yeah. Apparently it's really popular right now.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: demo kore, ichijikan wa matsu yo. nimotsu omoi shi, kyou wa yameyou ka.
lines.ja: でもこれ、一時間は待つよ。荷物重いし、今日はやめようか。
lines.kana: でもこれ、いちじかんはまつよ。にもつおもいし、きょうはやめようか。
lines.english: But that's an hour's wait at least, and our bags are heavy. Shall we give it a miss today?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un. jaa, kono chikaku no kafe, ikanai? soko, hyouban ii n da yo.
lines.ja: うん。じゃあ、この近くのカフェ、行かない？そこ、評判いいんだよ。
lines.kana: うん。じゃあ、このちかくのかふぇ、いかない？そこ、ひょうばんいいんだよ。
lines.english: Okay. Then how about a café near here? It's got a really good reputation.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hee. demo, ninki aru nara, soko mo hito ooi n ja nai?
lines.ja: へえ。でも、人気あるなら、そこも人多いんじゃない？
lines.kana: へえ。でも、にんきあるなら、そこもひとおおいんじゃない？
lines.english: Oh yeah? But if it's popular, won't it be crowded there too?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: uun, ninki aru tte iu yori, hyouban no ii omise na no.
lines.ja: ううん、人気あるっていうより、評判のいいお店なの。
lines.kana: ううん、にんきあるっていうより、ひょうばんのいいおみせなの。
lines.english: No, it's not so much popular as well thought of.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: itta hito wa minna yokatta tte iu kedo, omise wa sonna ni konde nai n da tte.
lines.ja: 行った人はみんなよかったって言うけど、お店はそんなに混んでないんだって。
lines.kana: いったひとはみんなよかったっていうけど、おみせはそんなにこんでないんだって。
lines.english: Everyone who's been says it was great, but apparently it doesn't get that packed.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.ja: そっか。じゃあ、そっち行ってみよう。
lines.kana: そっか。じゃあ、そっちいってみよう。
lines.english: I see. Let's try that one, then.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: koko da yo. ii fun'iki desho?
lines.ja: ここだよ。いい雰囲気でしょ？
lines.kana: ここだよ。いいふんいきでしょ？
lines.english: Here it is. Nice vibe, right?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: un, sugoku ii. a, mite, pankeeki mo aru!
lines.ja: うん、すごくいい。あ、見て、パンケーキもある！
lines.kana: うん、すごくいい。あ、みて、ぱんけーきもある！
lines.english: Yeah, really nice. Oh, look, they've got pancakes too!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.ja: ほんとだ。並ばなくてよかったね。
lines.kana: ほんとだ。ならばなくてよかったね。
lines.english: Oh, they do. Good thing we didn't queue.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: oishii! fun'iki mo ii shi, hyouban ii no, wakaru naa.
lines.ja: おいしい！雰囲気もいいし、評判いいの、わかるなあ。
lines.kana: おいしい！ふんいきもいいし、ひょうばんいいの、わかるなあ。
lines.english: So good! And it's got a lovely feel. I can see why people rave about it.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: desho? demo, minna ni wa naisho ni shite ne. koko mo hito ooku nattara, iya da kara.
lines.ja: でしょ？でも、みんなには内緒にしてね。ここも人多くなったら、嫌だから。
lines.kana: でしょ？でも、みんなにはないしょにしてね。ここもひとおおくなったら、いやだから。
lines.english: Right? But keep it to yourself, okay? I don't want this place getting crowded too.

choices.english: Mai takes Yuki to a café everyone is talking about, but it's packed as well, so they head home with their bags.
They queue for an hour at the popular pancake place, then decide a quieter café nearby would have been better.
They skip the long line at the popular pancake place and go to a quieter, well-reviewed café, which has pancakes too.

questions.explanation: Line 4: Mai points out the huge line at the pancake place they'd planned to visit, and line 6 says it's really popular right now. Line 7: Yuki says it's at least an hour's wait and their bags are heavy, so they give it a miss. Line 8: Mai suggests a café nearby with a good reputation, and line 12 says it doesn't get that packed. In lines 15-16 they find it has pancakes too and are glad they didn't queue. A is wrong: Yuki worries the café will be crowded (line 9), but Mai says it isn't (line 12), and they stay and eat there (line 17). B is wrong: they never join the queue. Yuki suggests skipping it in line 7, and Mai agrees in line 8.

questions.english: Your friend Kenta asks you, "nee, doyoubi ni ano pankeeki no omise, ikanai?" Say Saturdays are crowded and suggest another time, using hito ga ooi.
questions.ja: ねえ、土曜日にあのパンケーキのお店、行かない？
questions.kana: ねえ、どようびにあのぱんけーきのおみせ、いかない？
questions.romaji: nee, doyoubi ni ano pankeeki no omise, ikanai?
questions.answer: Say Saturdays are crowded with hito ga ooi (in casual speech, hito ooi), give it as your reason with kara, and suggest another time.

modelAnswers.romaji: doyoubi wa hito ooi kara, kin'youbi no yoru ni shinai?
modelAnswers.ja: 土曜日は人多いから、金曜日の夜にしない？
modelAnswers.english: Saturdays are crowded, so why don't we go Friday night instead?

modelAnswers.romaji: ii yo. demo doyoubi wa hito ga ooi kara, asa hayaku ikou.
modelAnswers.ja: いいよ。でも土曜日は人が多いから、朝早く行こう。
modelAnswers.english: Sure. But it's crowded on Saturdays, so let's go early in the morning.

questions.explanation: In line 3 Yuki says 'nanka kyou, hito ooi ne' (it's crowded today), and Mai answers that it's Saturday (doyoubi da kara ne). In line 9 Yuki asks 'soko mo hito ooi n ja nai?' (won't it be crowded there too?), and in line 18 Mai says 'hito ooku nattara' (if it gets crowded). The people are the subject and ooi comes after them, so don't say 'ooi hito ga iru' for 'there are lots of people'. Before a noun it's takusan no hito. Don't call a place isogashii (busy) either: crowded is hito ga ooi or konderu, as in line 12 (konde nai). Kenta is a friend, so a casual answer fits.

questions.english: You walk past the pancake place with your little brother Kenji, and he asks, "nee, nande ano mise, anna ni naranderu no?" Tell him why, using ninki ga aru.
questions.ja: ねえ、なんであの店、あんなに並んでるの？
questions.kana: ねえ、なんであのみせ、あんなにならんでるの？
questions.romaji: nee, nande ano mise, anna ni naranderu no?
questions.answer: Say the place is popular: ninki ga aru, with ga dropped in casual speech (ninki aru). Add n da tte if it's something you've heard, or n da yo if you're telling him.

modelAnswers.romaji: saikin, sugoku ninki aru n da tte.
modelAnswers.ja: 最近、すごく人気あるんだって。
modelAnswers.english: Apparently it's really popular right now.

modelAnswers.romaji: ano mise, ima sugoku ninki ga aru n da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: あの店、今すごく人気があるんだよ。
modelAnswers.english: That place is really popular at the moment.

questions.explanation: Mai says the first model answer word for word in line 6, about the same long line. A queue like that means lots of people like the place and go there, which is ninki ga aru. Line 10 sets it against hyouban ga ii (people speak well of it), which doesn't need a crowd. Don't say popyuraa: in Japanese it's for things that are widely known or standard, not a shop people flock to. Kenji is your little brother, so answer casually.

questions.english: When they get to the café, what does Mai say about it?
questions.ja: マイさんは、カフェのことを何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、かふぇのことをなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, kafe no koto o nan to iimashita ka?
questions.explanation: Line 14: 'koko da yo. ii fun'iki desho?' fun'iki is the feel of a place, so ii fun'iki is a nice vibe. In line 17 Yuki says it with the noun first, 'fun'iki mo ii shi', which is just as natural. A is wrong: ii kuuki means fresh air. kuuki is only a mood in set phrases like kuuki o yomu (read the room) and kuuki ga omoi (an awkward mood). C is wrong: in line 10 Mai says the café isn't so much popular (ninki aru tte iu yori) as well thought of, and in line 12 that it doesn't get packed. ninki aru is what she said about the pancake place (line 6).

questions.english: Mai says the café is "ninki aru tte iu yori, hyouban no ii omise." What kind of place is it?
questions.ja: そのカフェは、どんなお店ですか？
questions.kana: そのかふぇは、どんなおみせですか？
questions.romaji: sono kafe wa, donna omise desu ka?

choices.english: People who've been there speak well of it, but it doesn't get crowded.
So many people go there that it's always packed.
Everyone has heard of it, but people say it isn't very good.

questions.explanation: Line 10 sets the two apart: not so much ninki aru (popular) as hyouban no ii omise (a place people speak well of). Line 12 explains: everyone who's been says it was good (itta hito wa minna yokatta tte iu), but it doesn't get that packed. That's hyouban ga ii: it's about what people say. Before a noun ga becomes no, as in hyouban no ii omise. Mai first says it in line 8 (hyouban ii n da yo), and Yuki agrees in line 17. B is ninki ga aru, what Mai says about the pancake place (line 6) and what Yuki wrongly expects of the café in line 9. C is wrong: that would be hyouban ga warui, the opposite. And being widely known is yuumei (famous), which nobody says here.

questions.english: You meet Mai in the street with two big shopping bags, and she sighs, "neko no gohan, mata takusan katchatta." Offer to help, using nimotsu ga omoi.
questions.ja: 猫のごはん、またたくさん買っちゃった。
questions.kana: ねこのごはん、またたくさんかっちゃった。
questions.romaji: neko no gohan, mata takusan katchatta.
questions.answer: Say her bags must be heavy with nimotsu ga omoi (in casual speech, nimotsu omoi desho?), then offer to carry one: hitotsu motou ka?

modelAnswers.romaji: nimotsu omoi desho? hitotsu motou ka?
modelAnswers.ja: 荷物重いでしょ？一つ持とうか？
modelAnswers.english: Your bags must be heavy. Want me to take one?

modelAnswers.romaji: uwa, nimotsu omosou. hitotsu motsu yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うわ、荷物重そう。一つ持つよ。
modelAnswers.english: Whoa, those bags look heavy. Let me take one.

questions.explanation: Line 1: Yuki offers to carry one of Mai's bags (nimotsu, hitotsu motou ka?), and in line 2 Mai says 'nimotsu sugoku omoi n da' (my bags are really heavy). In line 7 Yuki uses 'nimotsu omoi shi' as a reason to skip the queue. The bags are the subject, nimotsu ga omoi, and ga usually drops in casual speech. Before a noun it's omoi nimotsu. omosou means 'looks heavy'. Mai is a friend, so answer casually.

newWords.english: line up, queue (naranderu: there's a line)
